## Pre-sweep against the post-S3 tree (`impl-8257` @ `9424881459c`), before spending a gate run

### DEFECT — a cross-epic rename breaks 2 citations, and nothing links the 2 stories

This plan names `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py` twice:

1. the Approach note — "`test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py` does not history-exempt `infra/runbooks/`"
2. the Testing section's `pytest …` invocation, which passes it as an explicit path

**That file is renamed out from under this story by `b721-6c6d-504e-45da`** ("Rename the 76 unpaired held-out test modules to drop the `_heldout` suffix"). Measured: it has no same-directory base twin, so it is unpaired, and it sits in the `interfaces` tier that b721's own split counts as 18 of the 76. b721's stated end state is that `tests/**/test_*_heldout.py` matches nothing. After b721 it is `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale.py`.

**The two stories are in different epics (`cdac` vs `6ed2`) with no dependency link in either direction**, so landing order is unconstrained. If b721 lands first, the Testing command fails with a path error — a self-inflicted red that has nothing to do with this story's work.

Suggested fix: cite the module by its stem and let the path follow, or state both names. The cheap form is to invoke it as `tests/interfaces/contracts/ -k bridge_vocabulary_stale`, which survives the rename either way.

### The 3 ranges the plan deferred — re-measured, so they are not an implementation-time discovery

The plan says line numbers for ADRs 0031 and 0085 are pre-S3 and must be "re-measured and restated as the first implementation step". Done here, against S3's actual tree:

| citation | plan (pre-S3) | post-S3 | shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR 0031 `### Operator break-glass` | `:158-165` | **`:160-167`** | +2 |
| ADR 0085 `### 3. Eventual-consistency discipline…` | `:58-71` | **`:60-73`** | +2 |
| ADR 0085 `### 4. Report` | `:73-79` | **`:75-81`** | +2 |

Boundaries confirmed by printing them rather than inferring: in 0031 the content ends at `:167` ("lease interval automatically."), `:168` is blank, and `## Lease self-healing (C2 — extends this module)` is at `:169`. In 0085, §3 ends at `:73`, `:74` blank, `### 4. Report` at `:75`; §4 ends at `:81`, `:82` blank, `## Consequences` at `:83`.

**The shift is uniformly +2 on all 3**, consistent with S3 inserting a 2-line archive banner (banner + blank) above each body. The plan's own warning was correct, and its instinct to anchor on headings rather than numbers is what makes this re-measurement trivial.

### Citations that hold — 14 of 14 checked

| claim | result |
|---|---|
| `infra/runbooks/` holds 21 runbooks | **21** ✓ |
| `scripts/run_live_matrix.py:2` says "ADR 0037 §4" | exact ✓ |
| `review-bot-ops.md:252` `## The reconciler cursor` | exact ✓ |
| `:374` `## Kill-switch: revert the LLM path from Bedrock…` | exact ✓ |
| `:522` `## Continuous auto-deploy (epic 88ab / story 8903)` | exact ✓ |
| `:563` `**Back-out (disable auto-deploy):**` | exact ✓ |
| `:876`, `:1008`, `:1127`, `:1240` — the four `ADR 0112 / story …` cap sections | all 4 exact ✓ |
| `docs/config.md:657`, `:676` cite ADR 0112 | both ✓ |
| ADR 0112 `## Open items` at `:241` | exact ✓ |
| ADR 0105 `:94-97` one-time operator cutover bullet | exact ✓ |

### The history-exemption claim holds, and is sharper than the plan states

`_HISTORY_PREFIXES` is `("docs/adr/", "docs/archive/", "docs/experiments/", "evals/", "reports/stability/")`; `infra/` appears nowhere in the module. So the plan is right that `infra/runbooks/` is not exempt.

Worth making explicit, because it is the actual hazard in this story's shape: **`docs/adr/` IS exempt and `infra/runbooks/` is not.** Every line this story moves therefore crosses from exempt to scanned territory. Any retained old spelling sitting unnoticed in those 10 ADR bodies becomes a test failure the moment it lands in a runbook. The plan's "New runbooks use current vocabulary only" covers it, provided the rule is applied to *moved* text and not only to newly written text.

## Plan corrected ahead of review — 2 defects from the pre-sweep applied

Description is now 7,915 chars (was 7,638; an intermediate draft hit 8,314 and the editor correctly
refused it against the 8,000-char plan-review admission cap, so the historical `:158-168` note was

### 1. The Testing command cited a path that story `b721-6c6d-504e-45da` renames

`b721` ("Rename the 76 unpaired held-out test modules to drop the `_heldout` suffix") renames
`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py` **in place** to
`test_bridge_vocabulary_stale.py`. It is unpaired, so it is in that rename set, and it is not one of

(`cdac` and `6ed2`) with no dependency link, so landing order is unconstrained — if `b721` lands
first, this story's own Testing command fails on a missing path.

Replaced with a selector that collects the same tests under either name. Verified on `938e962c5d8`:

```
pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/ -k bridge_vocabulary_stale --collect-only -q
9/429 tests collected (420 deselected)
```

All 9 come from that module.

### 2. The selector had to become its own invocation

Folding `-k` into the existing 4-module `pytest` call would have silently deselected the other 3
modules, because `-k` filters the entire run rather than the argument it follows. Measured:

```
pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_docs.py tests/interfaces/contracts/ -k bridge_vocabulary_stale --collect-only -q
9/430 tests collected (421 deselected)

```

That 1 test is deselected by the combined form. The Testing section now runs the 3 module paths in
one invocation and the selector in a second.

### 3. Vocabulary rule widened from "new text" to "moved text"

The rule read "New runbooks use current vocabulary only". The scan's `_HISTORY_PREFIXES` exempts
`docs/adr/` but not `infra/runbooks/`, so every line this story moves crosses from unscanned into
scanned territory. The constraint now applies to moved prose explicitly, not only newly written
prose.

The ADR 0031 and 0085 line ranges stay as written with the existing instruction to re-measure as
the first implementation step, because they are measured pre-`8257` and `8257` shifts them. The
